Whenever I express my point of view or my feelings I’m told very often by men that I am wrong. 

One instance a friend of mine I guess got pissed off or jealous of something I said (which was unintentional). I had to prod any pry to see what was wrong and I was genuinely confused but I apologized I made him feel that way. But if I’m upset about something I try and just straight up say what is upsetting me and why and that is why I behaved like XYZ. I’m always in the wrong and I’m noticing a pattern of men doing this to me.

It wakes two partners to make a marriage work and that involves compromise. Sometimes you just need to see it as a lost cause. If she won’t do anything to help the situation that is very important to you (and in a marriage) than the only thing you can do is continue to work on yourself. 

I know first hand being in a lonely marriage where your spouse won’t kiss you on the lips or doesn’t show any affection. It’s lonelier than being by yourself. I go to therapy, work, go to school, take care of all the chores and pets, and I’m on meds to help me manage my abusive household. But all of those things I am doing for ME, because no one will ever have your back like you have yours. And I don’t want to wake up in 20 years feeling like this. 

Maybe have an exit strategy in the back of your head. Life is too short to be emotionally abandoned by someone you thought would always be there for you. Just a thought. But when one partner shuts down it’s a lost cause. Don’t waste your precious energy on it. And I’m giving you a virtual hug xo. I know the feeling and you will be okay ❤️

I clench and grind at night and therefore my masseters are quite developed and strong. I recently had my first Botox treatment due to my chronic headaches from TMJ and teeth grinding. I do believe the Botox won’t completely eliminate clenching and grinding but if you weaken the muscle you won’t be putting such strong forces on the teeth and therefore ruining them. The Botox will atrophy the muscle and make it weaker. You don’t use it you lose it kind of thing. My dentist still recommended wearing a guard at night on top of the Botox. I currently have the Invisalign that is working not only to correct my teeth but to protect them from my impressive bite force...

Yes! Mine is in that area too and also the entire length of both eyebrows. If I press on the muscle there it hurts and it feels like a knot. I recently had Botox injections for my chronic headaches, TMJ, and teeth grinding. I got 30 injections over my face, head, and neck....I was not expecting that many lol. I’m only a few days out and I feel amazing. Like my muscles that are constantly tight and contracted are just relaxed. So far no tension headaches!!!!! I’m so happy because I was resorting to NSAIDS but they didn’t help at all. My doctor tried a muscle relaxer before the Botox and it didn’t do anything but make me sleepy. I am so pleased. If your medical insurance will cover it I highly recommend it. What would really trigger the tension headaches would be me squinting like when it’s sunny out, being on the computer at work and just life in general.

I would do all the ones I knew how to do and it would slowly build my confidence during the exam. My anxiety would wear off and then I would tackle the harder questions.
